response.sql: WITH city_attendees AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(*) as attendee_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code GROUP BY z.city), city_shares AS (SELECT city, attendee_count, CAST(attendee_count AS FLOAT) / (SELECT SUM(attendee_count) FROM city_attendees) as share FROM city_attendees), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_val FROM city_shares) SELECT city, attendee_count, share, share - (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_share) as diff_from_avg FROM city_shares UNION ALL SELECT 'ABOVE_AVERAGE_SUMMARY', AVG(attendee_count), AVG(share), AVG(share - (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_share)) FROM city_shares WHERE share > (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_share);

assumptions.assumption: All members attending events have zip codes that exist in the zip_code table (no null or orphaned foreign keys in the join).
Attendees are counted per attendance record (each attendance row is one attendee count), not by distinct members. A member attending multiple events counts multiple times.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct members per city rather than attendance records (each member from a city counts once regardless of how many events they attended).
alternatives.sql: WITH city_attendees AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) as attendee_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code GROUP BY z.city), city_shares AS (SELECT city, attendee_count, CAST(attendee_count AS FLOAT) / (SELECT SUM(attendee_count) FROM city_attendees) as share FROM city_attendees), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_val FROM city_shares) SELECT city, attendee_count, share, share - (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_share) as diff_from_avg FROM city_shares UNION ALL SELECT 'ABOVE_AVERAGE_SUMMARY', AVG(attendee_count), AVG(share), AVG(share - (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_share)) FROM city_shares WHERE share > (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_share);
